question.text: Operational due diligence on an AIF focuses primarily on:

answer.text: Operations and management, AMC organisational structure, back-office personnel, internal controls, compliance, fraud-related proceedings, third-party service providers, and data-confidentiality controls

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook frames fund due diligence around operations and management, AMC organisational structure, back-office personnel, internal audit/control weaknesses, fraud or misrepresentation proceedings, third-party service providers, compliance issues, and distributor confidentiality/cyber/data-theft controls. These together describe operational due diligence for an AIF. The Trap: Operational due diligence is distinct from investment performance review. Even a fund that picks well can harm investors through weak controls, compliance gaps, or service-provider issues. Note: Earlier wording used a generic operational-risk definition (inadequate internal processes, systems, personnel errors, external events) and examples such as NAV errors, cybersecurity breaches, disaster recovery plans, and fund blowups. Those are broader than the checked workbook and have been replaced with the source-listed due-diligence and control items.
